meta.title: Why I Wash my Meat Before Stir-Frying | Kenji’s Cooking Show
meta.description:
You can order my book The Wok: Recipes and Techniques here: www.kenjilopezalt.com

Donate to No Kid Hungry here: https://p2p.onecause.com/livestreamfornokidhungry/kenji-alt-lopez

Here is my older beef and broccoli video, which does not feature the washing step I demonstrate in this video. Adding the washing step would improve the texture of the beef in the original beef and broccoli video: https://youtu.be/iEs3qXQvg6M

Here’s Wang Gang’s channel: https://youtube.com/channel/UCg0m_Ah8P_MQbnn77-vYnYw

great but the key is really to cut it against the grain so you can see that the muscle fibers run in this direction and so you want to cut across that and i like to cut at a little bit of an angle like this so that you get a little more surface area so the idea here is that by cutting against the grain you're shortening the muscle fibers so that they aren't just tough there are some times when
